Whoever has eaten garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
Gathering kabath fruit, the Prophet said the black ones are better, and when asked if he had shepherded sheep, said every prophet had done so.
After eating, the Prophet rinsed his mouth and prayed without new ablution; lick fingers before wiping them; he praised Allah after meals; a servant who cooked should get a share.
Seeing hunger on the Prophet's face, Abu Shu'aib had a meal for five made; when a sixth man followed, the Prophet left it to him, and he admitted the man.
Called to prayer, the Prophet left his mutton and prayed without renewing ablution; when supper is served as the Isha iqama is called, supper comes first, as Ibn Umar did.
Guests lingered after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh; when they left he hung a curtain before Anas, and the verse of Hijab was revealed.
The Prophet put chewed dates in newborns' mouths and blessed them, among them Asma's son Abdullah bin az-Zubair, and named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim and Abu Talha's son Abdullah.
Aqiqa is offered for a newborn boy, with an animal slaughtered and his suffering relieved; Fara' and Atira, the pagans' firstling for idols and the Rajab sheep, are not permitted.
Game killed by a Mi'rad's edge or a trained hound sent with Allah's name may be eaten, not if struck by its side or another dog joined; stone-throwing hunts nothing.
Whoever keeps a dog not for hunting or guarding livestock loses two qirats of reward each day.
Game a trained hound sent with Allah's name catches is lawful unless it ate or other hounds joined; arrow-shot game found days later may be eaten unless in water.
Anas caught a rabbit whose legs the Prophet accepted; Abu Qatada, not in Ihram, killed an onager alone, and the Prophet told companions in Ihram it was food from Allah.
Troops ate a fish the sea cast up, and locusts; People of the Scripture's vessels are used, washed, only if no others exist; domestic donkey meat at Khaibar was discarded.
Any blood-letting tool may slaughter, with Allah's name, except tooth or nail, and a runaway camel may be shot; Zaid bin Amr refused meat slaughtered on stone altars.
Those who slaughtered their sacrifice before the Eid prayer were told to slaughter another; others were to slaughter after it, mentioning Allah's name.
A dying sheep slaughtered with a stone was allowed; any blood-letting tool serves except tooth or nail; meat from recent converts is eaten with Allah's name said over it.
Besieging Khaibar, Abdullah bin Mughaffal went to take a skin of fat thrown down, then, seeing the Prophet behind him, held back out of shyness.
Facing battle without knives, they were told any blood-letting tool serves except tooth or nail and a runaway camel may be shot; Asma's people slaughtered a horse and ate it.
Anas and Ibn Umar, seeing boys shoot at a tied hen, said the Prophet forbade killing tied animals, cursed mutilating a live one, and forbade An-Nuhba.
Abu Musa saw the Prophet eating chicken.
Abu Musa urges a man who swore off chicken to eat it, recalling that the Prophet, having sworn to give no mounts, gave them, doing what is better and expiating.
Donkey meat and Mut'a marriage were forbidden at Khaibar, horse meat allowed, though Ibn Abbas withheld a verdict on donkeys; fanged beasts are forbidden; a dead sheep's hide is usable.
Whoever is wounded in Allah's cause will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound bleeding, its colour that of blood and its smell that of musk.
A good companion is like a musk-carrier, who gives, sells or lets you smell musk; a bad one like a bellows-blower, who burns your clothes or leaves a stench.
The Prophet accepted a rabbit's legs and neither ate nor forbade mastigure, unknown in his land; butter-fat is eaten once a dead mouse and the fat around it are discarded.
Ibn Umar disliked branding animals on the face, as the Prophet forbade striking the face, while Anas saw the Prophet branding a sheep, on its ear he thought.
Without knives, slaughter with anything that makes blood flow, naming Allah, but not tooth or nail; a camel bolting like a wild beast may be stopped with an arrow.
Sacrifice follows the Eid prayer, earlier slaughter being only meat; Abu Burda and Uqba were allowed young animals, and the Prophet sacrificed two rams, and cows for his wives.
On the day of Nahr the Prophet names the four sacred months, declares blood, property and honour sacred, forbids killing one another, and has those present inform the absent.
The Prophet slaughtered at the Musalla and sacrificed two horned black-and-white rams himself; a sacrifice before the Eid prayer is repeated, Abu Burda's young goat sufficing for him only.
The Prophet sent garlanded sacrificial animals to the Ka'bah without avoiding anything lawful; sacrificial meat, banned beyond three days in a hard year, was later allowed to be stored.
Umar relayed the Prophet's ban on fasting the two Eids, Ali his ban on sacrificial meat after three days; at a Friday Eid, Uthman let suburb-dwellers go home before Jumua.
The Prophet said to eat sacrificial meat for three days, so Ibn Umar, leaving Mina, ate bread with oil rather than the meat of the Hadi.
Whoever drinks alcohol unrepentant is denied it hereafter; the Prophet chose milk over wine on his night journey; drinking portends the Hour, and a drinker is no believer while drinking.
Banned alcohol, mostly made from dates, was poured out; Umar said it comes from five things and clouds the mind; all intoxicants are unlawful, though some will deem them lawful.
Abu Usaid's bride soaked dates overnight for the Prophet's drink; he forbade certain drink containers, such as Ad-Dubba', Al-Muzaffat and green jars, then allowed some to those in need.
Any intoxicating drink is unlawful whatever its name, while the Prophet liked sweets and honey; drinks of mixed dates counted as alcohol, and mixing fruits for a drink was forbidden.
The Prophet chose milk on his ascent, drank it at Arafat and from Abu Bakr on leaving Mecca, said to cover it, rinsed after it, and praised lending milch animals.
Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden, where the Prophet drank, in charity when the verse on spending what one loves came, dividing it among his kin as advised.
The Prophet drank milk mixed with water and passed it to his right, even a boy before elders; he liked sweets and honey, and he and Ali drank water standing.
